note: Realistic filled-in states in the scoring engine's shape. `expected` is computed by `bin/test-personas --update` and verified by `bin/test-personas`.

personas.name: normal-complete-study
personas.description: Normal awake EEG with a normal background rhythm and no structured findings — every axis at baseline on a complete report.

state.clinicalHistory: First unprovoked seizure-like episode query syncope; routine EEG requested
state.findingsNarrative: Normal alpha background rhythm, reactive to eye opening. No epileptiform discharges, no focal or generalised slowing. Hyperventilation and photic stimulation unremarkable.
state.clinicalCorrelation: No electrographic correlate of the reported episode captured during the recording.
state.recommendedFollowUp: None required from a neurophysiology perspective

expected.recommendedAction: No specific neurophysiology follow-up required; manage per usual care.

firedRules.description: No abnormal structured or background findings on an interpretable recording; classified as normal.
No abnormal finding; abnormality severity graded none.
No escalation rule fired; routine follow-up only.

personas.name: minor-excess-slow-background-incidental
personas.description: An isolated excess-slow background rhythm with no other structured findings — minor severity from the background abnormality alone, reported as an incidental finding rather than an actionable one (the incidental-finding flag requires no focal/generalised slowing alongside it).

state.clinicalHistory: Non-specific dizzy spells, no clear seizure semiology
state.findingsNarrative: Mild excess of theta activity in the background, otherwise a well-organised recording. No epileptiform discharges or focal abnormality.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Non-specific finding; can be seen with drowsiness or mild encephalopathy.
state.impression: Mild non-specific background slowing, an incidental finding.
state.recommendedFollowUp: No specific action required; correlate clinically if symptoms persist

expected.recommendedAction: Correlate the minor background abnormality with the clinical context and follow up as indicated.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured or background findings are present; classified as abnormal.
A minor background abnormality (excess slowing or asymmetry) only; abnormality severity graded minor.
Mandatory report section missing: comparison with previous EEG.
Minor background abnormality; structured follow-up recommended.

flags.description: A minor background abnormality is documented as an incidental finding.
flags.suggestedAction: Correlate the minor background abnormality with the clinical context.

personas.name: moderate-focal-slowing-actionable-no-flag
personas.description: Isolated focal slowing with no other structured findings — moderate severity via the actionable-finding rule, but notably raises no dedicated safety flag of its own (unlike the seizure/status-epilepticus triggers below), since focal slowing sits outside every flags.js condition; a real, verified gap between the severity grading and the flag set.

state.clinicalHistory: Focal-onset seizure semiology with left-sided jerking; interictal EEG
state.findingsNarrative: Intermittent focal slowing over the right temporal region, without epileptiform discharges. Background otherwise normal.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Non-specific for a structural lesion in the right temporal region; correlate with imaging.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Neurology review; correlate with MRI if not already performed

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend neurology review or a follow-up recording as clinically indicated.

firedRules.description: One or more abnormal structured or background findings are present; classified as abnormal.
An actionable abnormal finding (focal slowing, generalised slowing, photoparoxysmal response, or abnormal background) is present; severity graded moderate.
Mandatory report section missing: comparison with previous EEG.

personas.name: moderate-photoparoxysmal-response-urgent-referral
personas.description: A photoparoxysmal response to photic stimulation with no other structured findings — moderate severity via the actionable-finding rule, and raises the urgent-referral flag (photoparoxysmal response is one of its two triggers).

state.clinicalHistory: Teenager with episodes triggered by flashing lights at a concert
state.findingsNarrative: A generalised photoparoxysmal response was elicited during photic stimulation at 16 Hz. Background otherwise normal.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Consistent with a photosensitive epilepsy trait; correlates with the reported flashing-light-triggered episodes.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Urgent neurology / epilepsy clinic referral; photosensitivity precautions advice

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend neurology review or a follow-up recording as clinically indicated.

flags.description: A recorded seizure or photoparoxysmal response is present and may warrant urgent neurology referral.
flags.suggestedAction: Consider urgent referral to the neurology / epilepsy team.

personas.name: moderate-abnormal-background-rhythm
personas.description: An abnormal background rhythm (neither simply excess-slow nor asymmetric, but qualitatively disorganised) with no other structured findings — moderate severity via the abnormal-background branch of the actionable rule, and raises no dedicated flag (a second real gap between the moderate-severity grading and the flag set, distinct from the focal-slowing persona above).

state.clinicalHistory: Encephalopathy of uncertain cause, mild confusion
state.findingsNarrative: Disorganised background with poor state changes and reduced reactivity, without focal or epileptiform features.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Consistent with a mild diffuse encephalopathy; correlate with metabolic and infective screen.
state.impression: Disorganised background consistent with mild encephalopathy.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Neurology review; correlate with metabolic and infective work-up

expected.recommendedAction: Recommend neurology review or a follow-up recording as clinically indicated.

personas.name: epileptiform-discharges-critical-composite
personas.description: Frequent epileptiform discharges with no recording duration documented and no originating request reference linked — the third critical trigger, stacking the missing-measurement and unexpected-finding flags alongside the two universal critical-result flags; not yet communicated.

state.clinicalHistory: Recurrent brief staring episodes with unresponsiveness in a school-age child
state.findingsNarrative: Frequent generalised 3Hz spike-and-wave discharges, several activated by hyperventilation, consistent with a generalised epilepsy syndrome.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Findings support a diagnosis of childhood absence epilepsy; the originating referral could not be matched in the requesting system.
state.impression: Frequent generalised spike-and-wave discharges, consistent with absence epilepsy.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Urgent paediatric neurology referral for antiepileptic treatment planning
state.clinicianNotes: Recording duration not logged by the technologist; requesting clarification

expected.recommendedAction: Communicate the critical result directly to the referrer now and document the conversation.

personas.name: seizure-recorded-critical-communicated
personas.description: An electrographic seizure captured during the recording, already communicated to the on-call neurology team — a real, verified contrast with the ECG/echocardiogram engines' pattern: here F-URGENT-REFERRAL-001 has no `!hasCriticalFinding` guard in flags.js, so it correctly co-fires alongside F-CRITICAL-RESULT-001 for the same recorded-seizure finding rather than being suppressed once the report is already critical.

state.clinicalHistory: Admitted with breakthrough seizures despite therapeutic antiepileptic levels
state.findingsNarrative: A single electrographic seizure of 45 seconds' duration was captured, arising from the left temporal region, with a corresponding brief clinical arrest of activity noted by the ward nurse.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Correlates temporally with the nurse-witnessed event logged on the seizure diary.
state.impression: One electrographic seizure captured, left temporal onset.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Immediate antiepileptic medication review by the neurology team
state.reportedTo: Dr Marcus Webb, on-call neurology registrar, by phone at the time of the event

personas.name: status-epilepticus-critical
personas.description: Non-convulsive status epilepticus — the most acute of the three critical triggers, with its own dedicated abnormal-requiring-action flag (F-ABNORMAL-ACTION-001) distinct from the seizure/epileptiform-discharge triggers; not yet communicated.

state.clinicalHistory: Persistently reduced consciousness on the intensive care unit, query non-convulsive status
state.findingsNarrative: Continuous generalised rhythmic epileptiform activity throughout the recording without return to a normal background, consistent with non-convulsive status epilepticus.
state.clinicalCorrelation: Explains the persistently reduced level of consciousness.
state.recommendedFollowUp: Immediate escalation to the treating ICU/neurology team for urgent anti-status treatment
